messages:
sophia: FYI — escalating a confusing error from a customer (Acme Corp). They posted a rerank request and got a 413 / "Payload Too Large" with no detail on what exactly is over limit. They sent 1 query + ~250 docs, total payload ~3.2MB. Request ID: abc123.

Customer paste of error: 
`HTTP/1.1 413 Payload Too Large`
`{ "error": "request too large" }`

They asked: is it docs count, tokens, characters, or serialized JSON size? They need clear guidance and a way to detect which docs caused the reject. Raising here to confirm current limits and get a suggested message to return.

sam: Can you paste the exact request body (sanitized) + headers? curious if they're sending base64 attachments or huge string fields. Also, is this the /v1/reranker endpoint?

sophia: Yep endpoint is POST /v1/rerank (customer copy). Here's a stripped-down repro payload they provided (removed actual doc text) — they sent items as array of objects: 

```json
{
  "query": "How do I configure X?",
  "docs": [ {"id":1, "text": "<~long doc 1>~>"}, {"id":2, "text": "<~long doc 2>~>"}, ... up to 250 entries ]
}
```

Headers: Content-Type: application/json, Authorization: Bearer <redacted>

They also tried smaller batches (50 docs) and it succeeded. So likely the per-request docs cap or total token cap.

sam: Thanks. Quick check in logs (dave?), any server-side details for abc123? if we surface which limit it hit we can give the customer exact guidance.


dave: I pulled the request traces for abc123. Backend returned 413 at the pre-parse stage. Stack notes: payload_size_bytes = 3225600, docs_count = 248, estimated_total_tokens ~ 91500 (client-side token estimation). Current enforced thresholds (recent config): per_doc_token_limit = 4096, per_request_token_limit = 65536, hard_doc_count_limit = 200. In this case docs_count > hard_doc_count_limit (248 > 200) so request rejected.

Body returned by runtime: 
`{ "error": "request too large" }` — no structured detail.

sophia: Ok that matches user behavior (50 worked, 250 failed). Two issues: 1) error text is too generic, 2) customers confuse token vs characters vs docs. They asked for a field like `over_limit: { docs: 248, allowed_docs: 200 }` or a list of doc indexes that caused the exceed.

nora: From product side — agreed we should return actionable info. Proposed error payload: 

```json
{
  "error": "request_too_large",
  "reason": "docs_count_exceeded",
  "details": {"docs_sent":248, "docs_allowed":200, "per_request_token_limit":65536}
}
```

Wording suggestions for support KB: short bullets explaining limits (docs-per-request, tokens per doc, total tokens), example of how to chunk, and a sample server response to expect — include tips: pre-filter with embeddings, pre-rank top-k, or call rerank in multiple batches.

sam: I can prototype a quick change to include structured details when we hit a hard limit (docs_count or token_total) — would be a small change in the validation layer. Quick plan: if docs_count > limit return 400 with reason docs_count_exceeded and details; if total_tokens > limit return reason tokens_exceeded and provide estimated counts. I can open a PR but need agreement on response shape and whether to leak token counts.


dave: SRE note — fine to return counts and reasons, but avoid exposing internal tokenization model specifics. Return estimates (client_estimated_tokens) when available, and server_estimated_tokens otherwise. Also note: changing response may affect client parsers — we should version it (e.g., include `schema_version: v1`). ops-bot: Next deploy window is in ~2 hours (low risk) — tag as hotfix? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

nora: Product approves the structured error as long as wording is clear and we include migration notes. Please include a one-sentence user-facing error that people will see in logs: 

`Error: Request exceeds per-request document limit (200). Reduce docs per request or submit in batches.`

sophia: I'll update the support response templates and KB. Draft note to send to customer: 

"Thanks — we found your request exceeded our per-request document cap of 200. You can either send fewer docs per request (<=200), or split into multiple rerank calls. We plan to update the API error to return a detailed reason and counts to make this clearer. Apologies for the confusion; we’ll follow up once the backend change lands." :white_check_mark:

sam: Opening PR now. I'll include unit tests and example payloads. Assigning to @sam, reviewer @dave.

dave: I'll schedule the deploy in the low-risk window and watch the metrics. If we see a spike of these 413s we should also consider raising the soft limit or adding a queue/backpressure for very large batched jobs.

sophia: Customer accepted the temporary guidance and will batch their requests. They asked how to detect this client-side — I'll add a short snippet in KB showing a pre-check: 

```js
// simple client pre-check pseudocode
function shouldSend(docs) {
  const DOC_LIMIT = 200;
  if (docs.length > DOC_LIMIT) return false;
  // optional: token estimate call or local tokenizer check
  return true;
}
```

nora: Action items summary: 1) sam PR to return structured limit errors (ETA 2h), 2) dave schedule deploy + monitor, 3) sophia update KB + customer template, 4) product to review wording post-merge.

ops-bot: Deployment scheduled: service: rerank-validation, window: 2026-03-15T22:00Z -> 22:15Z, changelist: CL-4521, oncall: dave.

sophia: Thanks all — closing this thread once PR is merged and KB is live.

sam: PR merged and staged. Will post link after canary completes.

dave: Canary looks green. Rolling to prod. Monitoring on.

sophia: Confirmed with customer and KB updated. Closing. :tada:
